200.title: EU approves €11.4 million grant for Poland-Germany biomass heating project
200.body: Home All News Biomass EU approves €11.4 million grant for Poland-Germany biomass heating project All News Biomass EU approves €11.4 million grant for Poland-Germany biomass heating project By Randhir Patil September 25, 2026 The European Commission has approved a €11.41 million ($12.98 million) grant to support a cross-border biomass district heating project serving Slubice in Poland and Frankfurt in Germany, Biomass Magazine reported. The funding will support the 2024-6-TWIN-HEAT project, which aims to fully decarbonise district heating in Slubice and initiate deep decarbonisation of the heating system in Frankfurt through a coordinated cross-border approach based on renewable energy sources. The project is intended to demonstrate how cross-border coordination and renewable energy-based district heating can support the decarbonisation of urban heating systems in neighbouring European cities.

400.body: Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe (PEJ), Westinghouse and Bechtel announced they have agreed the main terms and conditions of the construction contract for Poland's first nuclear power plant. The milestone comes as several European countries accelerate their own nuclear programs, following Italy, whose Senate approved the country's return to nuclear power, and the United Kingdom, which detailed reforms to speed up nuclear delivery. In September 2023, Westinghouse, Bechtel and PEJ - a special-purpose vehicle 100% owned by Poland's State Treasury - had signed an 18-month engineering services contract covering the finalization of a site-specific design.
